messages:
ellie: quick follow-up to the sandboxing RFC — thinking out loud about an async page-return path from tenant heaps back to host without global stop-the-world compaction. wondering if this sketch makes sense and what races i missed

jon: interested — can you paste the sketch?

ellie: sure. idea: each tenant heap gets a lightweight sandbox arena header with a monotonically increasing epoch. when we want to return cold pages we mark them as 'reclaiming' in the arena and enqueue descriptors to a per-node async return queue. host drains queues and runs reclamation without blocking allocs except brief CASes. pseudo:```json
{
  "arena_epoch": 42,
  "slot_state": "RECLAIMING",
  "return_queue": [ { "page_id": "p123", "tenant": "t45" } ]
}
```

alex: couple of immediate flags: 1) how do we prevent alloc racing with a page that's being returned? 2) need a GC barrier or refcount check.

maria: +1 to refcount. can we add a short-lived reservation token on hot pages to avoid thundering reclaims? like a fast refcount bump on access that prevents them from entering queue for X ms.

ellie: yes, plan was soft reservations: access increments soft_ref and a background sweeper ignores pages with soft_ref > 0. soft_ref wraps at 255 to avoid unbounded growth.

sam: what about cross-pool handoffs? if a tenant's stage pool migrates between nodes, queued returns might hit wrong host. need a hint in the descriptor with current owner or a tombstone check.

ellie: good point — include owner_epoch + pool_id in descriptor and check when draining. if mismatch push back to tenant queue with backoff.

lucy: do we plan to update accounting synchronously? if returns are async we risk temporarily double-counting memory. that'll break quota checks.

ellie: we can do a two-phase accounting: optimistic decrement when queued + final reconciliation when host completes return. that keeps quota conservative but avoids stalls. open to other ideas.

jon: sounds reasonable but we need to be careful with failures: host crash after optimistic decrement will leak quota. need a reconciliation sweep that reclaims 'in-flight' markers older than TTL.

infra-bot: note: created issue INF-3342 for reconciliation sweep TTL and ownership tombstones (link: https://redwood.example/INF-3342) :robot_face:

alex: implementation nit: prefer not to add per-page epoch fields because (a) metadata blowup, (b) cache pressure. maybe maintain a compact bloom/version vector per arena to test recent access instead of per-page counters.

maria: bloom is okay but false positives will keep cold pages resident longer. tradeoff between metadata cost and reclaim aggressiveness. we should measure on the 8G and 24G small-model workloads.

sam: also check behavior under hot multi-tenant spike — we don't want queues to grow unbounded. need backpressure: when queue > threshold pause reclaiming and trigger immediate compaction or tenant-level throttles.

ellie: agree. plan: threshold per-node + global shed policy. on overflow, mark tenant "reclaim-paused" and emit telemetry.

jon: can we simulate this quickly in the allocator simulator? add an 'async-return' toggle and run mixed-traffic 90/10 hot/cold traces. i can extend the sim this week.

ellie: awesome — will add test cases and a draft PR for the arena header, queue descriptor, and optimistic accounting. will also document failure modes.

alex: one last thought — API for private deployments: some customers need deterministic host-side returns. we should expose a config to force synchronous handoff (blocking) for compliance.

ellie: noted — sync-mode toggle + metrics. thanks everyone.

infra-bot: reminder: mention in RFC follow-up doc and add perf numbers once sim is in.

ellie: will do. TL;DR: sandboxed arena + async return queue + soft-ref + optimistic accounting + tombstones + backpressure. next: sim and perf thresholds. :thumbsup:
